A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same aspect-oriented summarization study for psychiatric readmission prediction. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original four-hospital experiments, including readmission prediction scores, repeated-training statistics, and comparisons of information signals across summary types.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports supervised full-note experiments with Qwen models and a hierarchical transformer.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains the same three summarization prompts, information-distance approach, merged and union datasets, and soft/any voting procedures. The added Qwen and hierarchical-transformer models are comparison methods, rather than new components of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four hospital datasets, patient eligibility criteria, and 30-day readmission task. Table 1 is unchanged. Appendix J's discussion of long-term outcomes introduces no evaluated task or population.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands supervised full-note comparisons by adding LoRA-tuned Qwen-2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen3-0.6B in Table 3, and a hierarchical transformer in Table 7. Section 5.3 also reports an unsuccessful raw-note Clinical Longformer experiment; its previously reported evaluations used summaries. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce 10-epoch LoRA training on full notes with development/test evaluation, and a raw-note Clinical Longformer trial using the first 4k tokens. Existing splits, metrics, and the 0.5 classification threshold remain unchanged. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that their protocols changed.

E4.justification: Appendix B and Figure 6 add a limited qualitative case showing the different content produced by three prompts for one psychiatric note. Existing information-distance, summary-integration, and prediction-distribution analyses are retained. The new hallucination discussion supplies no empirical hallucination test.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies sequential seeds starting at zero, including 0–4 for BiomedBERT, and Appendix C explicitly identifies the Qwen results as single-run. Previously reported repetition counts and Table 4's standard deviations are retained; there is no documented increase in runs or new significance testing.

E6.justification: V2 adds development/test results for both Qwen baselines and hierarchical-transformer scores across all four hospitals. For example, Table 3 reports Qwen-2.5's MGH test AUROC as 0.6109, and Table 7 reports hierarchical-transformer McLean AUROC as 0.5346. These substantially extend the reported baseline evidence. Matched original performance tables, including the relocated zero-shot results, remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.1 corrects the concordant-pair definition: when R1_i > R1_j, v1 incorrectly requires R2_i < R2_j, whereas v2 correctly requires R2_i > R2_j. The distance, dataset averaging, and integration equations otherwise retain their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: aspect-specific summaries contain different signals, prediction comparisons can measure those differences, and integrating summaries can improve downstream prediction. The additional baselines provide support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for weak full-note baselines, including limited data, possible overfitting or distribution mismatch, and input truncation. It also discusses hallucination propagation through the summarization pipeline and distinguishes short-term from long-term outcome prediction in Appendix J. These extend the qualifications around the retained central interpretations.

D1.justification: V1 provides model, library, and hardware information but omits essential training hyperparameters. V2 adds the learning-rate/epoch search, final learning rate 2e-5, 40 epochs, batch size 8, development-loss checkpoint selection, and CNLPT version 0.7.0. It also documents the new Qwen experiments' LoRA rank 12, q_proj/v_proj targets, and training duration. This substantially improves implementation documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial Related Work section covering prompt tuning, dynamic prompting, self-consistency, aspect-oriented summarization, clinical summarization, and patient outcome prediction. It explicitly positions measuring and combining complementary prompt signals relative to prompt-selection approaches, considerably expanding the earlier version's research context.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. V2 inserts related-work and discussion subsections, reorganizes appendix headings, shortens the zero-shot introduction, and makes local terminology, author-contact, and wording corrections. The revision principally adds material rather than extensively rewriting the existing account.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the displays: it splits the prompt figure between main text and appendix, relocates the zero-shot table and prediction-distribution plots, revises the Venn diagram's labels and sizing, and reformats appendix text into two columns. New displays include the sample summaries and two full-note baseline tables. Retained result displays preserve their underlying findings.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in reproducibility and comparative evaluation: Appendix D.1 supplies the previously missing training and checkpoint-selection recipe, while Tables 3 and 7 add supervised neural full-note alternatives to assess the summarization rationale. The corrected concordance definition and substantially expanded research positioning further improve assessability. The Qwen comparisons remain single-run and provide limited evidence for general claims about full-document modeling, but this limitation does not outweigh the substantial documentation and evaluation gains.
